name: SNR-blended epsilon/v target
tagline: Trains a sigmoid mixture of epsilon- and v-prediction whose blend weight ramps with log-SNR, then algebraically inverts the mixture for x0.
init_recovers: epsilon at high noise (w→0), v at low noise (w→1)
diff_from_baseline: Replaces the static epsilon / v / x0 baselines with a SNR-dependent convex combination of epsilon and v as the regression target, and inverts the resulting linear-in-x0 system in predict_x0. Other components (UNet, schedule, sampler) untouched.

name: Stabilized affine target
tagline: Predicts a delta-shifted convex blend $\sqrt{\bar\alpha+\delta}\,\epsilon + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha+\delta}\,x_0$, with a clamped algebraic inversion for sampling.

key_hyperparams.name: delta
key_hyperparams.role: shift added inside both square roots to bound coefficients away from 0

init_recovers: v-prediction up to a sign and shift when delta→0
diff_from_baseline: Differs from v-prediction by adding a constant offset under both square roots so neither weight collapses to 0 over the schedule, and clamps the inverted x0 to [-1,1]. The overall target is still linear in (eps, x0), so predict_x0 is a closed-form inversion.

name: Min-SNR rotated v target
tagline: Defines a Min-SNR-weighted rotated parameterization: the target is a rotated noise/x0 mix where the rotation is set so its variance equals min(SNR, gamma)*(1-alpha).
formula: $$ W_t = \min(\mathrm{SNR}_t, \gamma),\; C = \sqrt{W_t(1-\bar\alpha_t)},\; S = \sqrt{1 - C^2} $$ $$ \text{target} = (\sqrt{\bar\alpha_t} C + \sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t} S)\,\epsilon - (\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t} C - \sqrt{\bar\alpha_t} S)\,x_0 $$
init_recovers: v-prediction up to scaling when gamma→∞
diff_from_baseline: Generalizes v-prediction by injecting Min-SNR (gamma=5) directly into the target geometry: instead of weighting the loss after-the-fact, it builds an angle-parameterized {eps, x0} mix whose magnitude C is tied to clipped SNR. Sampling uses the matching analytic x0 inversion.

name: Epsilon - SNR-gated x0
tagline: Predicts $\epsilon - k\,\mathrm{gate}(t)\,x_0$ with a soft gate $1/(1{+}\mathrm{SNR})$ that boosts an x0 correction at high noise.
init_recovers: Epsilon prediction at k=0 or low-noise (SNR→∞, g→0)
diff_from_baseline: A perturbed epsilon target: subtracts a (1+SNR)^-1 weighted fraction of x0 from the noise prediction so the high-noise regime gets an extra clean-image regression signal. predict_x0 inverts the affine map exactly.

name: Alpha^{1/4}-rescaled epsilon
tagline: Predicts noise multiplied by $\sqrt{1-\bar\alpha_t}/\bar\alpha_t^{1/4}$, giving low-noise timesteps more weight than standard epsilon.
init_recovers: Epsilon prediction up to a per-timestep loss reweighting
diff_from_baseline: Same epsilon direction as the epsilon baseline but rescales each timestep's target by sqrt(1-alpha)/alpha^{1/4}. This is equivalent to MSE on epsilon with a 1/sqrt(alpha) weighting, focusing capacity on low-noise (high-SNR) timesteps that drive FID.
